name: Asia
summary: The largest and most populous continent, holding the highest mountains, the largest plateau (Tibet) and both the wettest (Mawsynram) and some of the driest places.

name: Africa
summary: The cradle of humanity, with the Sahara, the Sahel, the Congo rainforest and the Great Rift Valley.

name: North America
summary: Spans Arctic tundra to tropical rainforest; the Great Plains are one of the world's breadbaskets.

name: South America
summary: Home of the Amazon, the Andes (the longest continental range) and the Atacama, the driest non-polar desert.

name: Antarctica
lowest: Denman Glacier trough (−3,500 m below sea level, under ice)
summary: The coldest, windiest, driest and highest continent on average; holds ~70% of Earth's fresh water as ice.

name: Europe
summary: A small, densely populated continent with mild Atlantic-influenced climates and some of the most intensively farmed land.

name: Oceania
summary: The driest inhabited continent, with ancient, weathered, nutrient-poor soils and Pacific island nations.
